precepts.text: Those with Simon were persuaded for money to let the enemy go, and Judas slew the traitors.
precepts.point: Menelaus outbid him for the priesthood, and Jason turned and slew his own people. The seekers of the white man's glory do the same today.

note.label: All Skinfolk Ain't Kinfolk: Children of Darkness

precepts.why:
Simon was “a betrayer of the money, and of his country”, and he slandered Onias, the righteous high priest, trying to get him taken out to replace him. After him came Jason, Onias’s own brother, another house negro, who labored underhand to be high priest; and then Menelaus, Simon’s brother, who outbid Jason for the priesthood. Simon, Jason, Menelaus: all traitors of their own people.

The betrayal for money did not stop with them. When Maccabeus and his men “ran with violence upon the strong holds of the Idumeans”, they killed no fewer than twenty thousand, and about nine thousand fled into two very strong castles. Maccabeus left Simon, Joseph and Zaccheus to besiege them and went where he was needed more.

“Now they that were with Simon, being led with covetousness, were persuaded for money through certain of those that were in the castle, and took seventy thousand drachms, and let some of them escape.” The enemy in the castle bribed them: let us escape and we will pay you. They took the money and let them go.

When Maccabeus heard it, he “accused those men, that they had sold their brethren for money, and set their enemies free to fight against them.” They sold out their own brothers. “So he slew those that were found traitors, and immediately took the two castles.” That is what was done to traitors back then: they got death.

So from Simon slandering Onias to the men selling their brethren for seventy thousand drachms, it is the same spirit. All skinfolk ain’t kinfolk. There were always those among us making a covenant with hell and death for money and the white man’s favor, even until now.

note.label: False New Year: Doctrine Slayer - True Past Curses & Trauma

precepts.why:
“Then they that were with Maccabeus made supplication, and besought God that he would be their helper; and so they ran with violence upon the strong holds of the Idumeans”, “and slew all that fell into their hands, and killed no fewer than twenty thousand.” Nine thousand of the Idumeans fled into “two very strong castles, having all manner of things convenient to sustain the siege”, with food and supplies to keep them alive.

Maccabeus left Simon, Joseph and Zaccheus to besiege them. “Now they that were with Simon, being led with covetousness, were persuaded for money through certain of those that were in the castle, and took seventy thousand drachms, and let some of them escape.” Some of our people were paid off to let Esau escape.

Maccabeus “accused those men, that they had sold their brethren for money, and set their enemies free to fight against them.” Sold their brethren for money: financial idolaters. “So he slew those that were found traitors, and immediately took the two castles.” We killed traitors back then. Judas Iscariot killed himself.

moments.label: Blasphemers & Traitors: Judge Not Before the Time

points: They that were with Maccabeus laid siege against the fortress courageously for days; and they that were within, trusting to the strength of the place, blasphemed exceedingly, and uttered wicked words.
So blaspheming is uttering wicked words against the Lord. Cursing, reproaching, blaspheming: synonymous.

note.label: Blasphemers & Traitors: Judge Not Before the Time

points: They were at war. Maccabeus had to leave some of his men and go somewhere else where there was a hot fight.

“Now they that were with Simon, being led with covetousness, were persuaded for money”. A lot of you are going to leave for money. They “took seventy thousand drachms, and let some of them escape”: they let the enemies go, through money.

He accused those men “that they had sold their brethren for money, and set their enemies free to fight against them.” Many of you will sell out your brothers for money. The things written aforetime were written for our learning. Setting the enemy free is letting the white man have free reign in your mind, and it has already happened: a lot of brothers left and went back to the church.
“So he slew those that were found traitors”. They were found traitors; they became treacherous.
